message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the same ancestor that gave rise to all placental mammals.  
In other words, the lion and the zebra share a common ancestor that lived roughly 70–100 million years ago, a small, insect‑eating mammal that was the first member of the Laurasiatheria clade (the group that eventually produced carnivores, perissodactyls, cetartiodactyls, and others). This ancestor is often referred to simply as the last common ancestor of placental mammals (or of Laurasiatheria).
